topic: A neighbor wants to install a fence
text: I’ve heard the blacksmith’s hammering all day, the clang and bang of metal cutting into the quiet of our fields. It’s bad enough the rain’s been scarce and the soil's as hard as a mule’s head, but now Old Hundt wants to drive his posts into the earth like he’s marking out a lord’s estate. We’ve always shared this common, let the sheep graze where they will. Now he talks of boundaries and shutting gates, as if walls can stop the wind or keep the cold at bay. The saints preserve us from neighbors who forget the ways of the land. I’ve seen what it means when folk start dividing what should be for all. It’s a road to hunger and hard feelings, and I’ll be wondering how many of my own flock will find their hooves barred from the green.
